published.title: Tech and Science, 30 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

EU lawmakers slam new border force powers to surveil social media

Technology – POLITICO

The European Commission proposed giving Frontex explicit powers to monitor social media for content that aids or encourages illegal border crossings into the EU. The plan revives a 2019 tender scrapped over privacy concerns and risks placing online speech under a border agency’s surveillance.

EU prepares strict new safeguards for future members as Montenegro nears accession

EUalive

The EU is drafting a new safeguard mechanism to prevent future members from backsliding on EU law or blocking Union decisions, with Montenegro likely to be the first test case. The proposal marks a significant shift in accession policy, aiming to give Brussels rapid response tools against democratic backsliding.

Canada to join EU network of supercomputers

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

Canada will join the EU’s EuroHPC supercomputer network, enabling access to 14 supercomputers, 19 AI factories and 10 quantum computers for Canadian researchers and startups. The €8.2 billion EuroHPC Joint Undertaking will also build seven AI gigafactories next year, deepening transatlantic AI cooperation.

EU tells capitals to halt their national social media bans for a year

Technology – POLITICO

The European Commission ordered EU member states to pause national laws restricting social media access for minors for 12 months while Brussels finalises an EU-wide Kids Act. Austria and other capitals had pressed ahead with their own age limits, but the Commission insists on a unified standard for under-13s and under-15s.

Everything that went wrong with Spain’s high-speed railways

Horizon Europe – POLITICO

A preliminary investigation into Spain’s deadly high-speed rail crash points to a chain of failures after a signalling system malfunction, with human error and maintenance issues also under scrutiny. The accident, the second in eight months, has turned rail safety into a political liability ahead of Spain’s snap election.

Winning the AI race while protecting our rights

EUalive

The EU AI Office has begun enforcing the AI Act’s rules for the most powerful models, issuing its first formal requests for information to OpenAI and Anthropic after multiple loss-of-control incidents. Europe is using binding legal powers to require developers of frontier models to demonstrate that their safeguards work, even though it produces few such models itself.

published.title: Tech and Science, 26 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Europe’s satellite merger tests drive for space independence

Technology – POLITICO

The EU faces a strategic dilemma over a proposed €6.5 billion merger between Airbus, Leonardo and Thales to create a European satellite champion, code-named 'Bromo'. The merger aims to boost Europe’s strategic autonomy in space but could raise costs as the bloc builds its own secure satellite communications, a priority highlighted by recent Starshield throttling in Ukraine.

Thousands protest Czech government’s public media overhaul after rushed vote

EUalive

Thousands protested in Prague after the Czech government fast-tracked a bill to abolish household fees funding public television and radio, moving them to the state budget. Critics argue the change leaves Czech Television and Czech Radio vulnerable to political pressure, undermining media independence.

published.title: Tech and Science, 24 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

European CEOs warn against surrendering frontier AI to US and China

Technology – POLITICO

European tech CEOs including DeepL’s Jarek Kutylowski reject calls to abandon frontier AI model development, arguing the EU must secure the full AI value chain to avoid ceding economic and strategic ground to the US and China. The debate exposes a split in European AI strategy, with industry leaders pushing for sustained investment in homegrown models despite trailing competitors, raising questions about funding and industrial policy.

Key takeaways from Belgium’s royal visit to Kazakhstan: critical raw materials, the Middle Corridor and EU cooperation

EUalive

Belgium and Kazakhstan agreed to expand cooperation on critical raw materials, including a joint research and training centre with East Kazakhstan University to develop higher-value production and recycling. The partnership targets EU strategic autonomy in raw materials, linking Belgian expertise with Kazakh resources to strengthen supply chains for advanced technologies.

Inside the cyber flaw scramble that brought the AI threat to life 

Technology – POLITICO

A premature disclosure of a critical PHP flaw, discovered using AI tools, forced governments worldwide to issue urgent warnings and take websites offline, highlighting how AI amplifies cybersecurity risks. The incident demonstrates the fragility of global cybersecurity coordination in the AI era and the outsized consequences of process failures for European digital infrastructure.

published.title: Tech and Science, 23 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

EU prosecutors search far-right offices in European Parliament as National Rally surges in French polls

EUalive

The European Public Prosecutor’s Office searched offices linked to the far-right Patriots for Europe group in the European Parliament over alleged misuse of €4.3 million in EU funds by its predecessor, the Identity and Democracy group. The investigation targets the misuse of EU funds by a former political group, involving offices connected to a current far-right party with Flemish ties.

Von der Leyen’s coalition fractures over need for AI liability rules

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

Centrist parties in the European Parliament clashed over whether to reintroduce AI liability rules, with the centre-left pushing for accountability for AI-driven harm and the centre-right prioritising simplification to boost competitiveness. The debate signals a fracture in the EU’s approach to AI governance, with direct implications for future regulation and liability frameworks.

Germany leads push against EU’s ‘associate membership’ label for Canada

Horizon Europe – POLITICO

Germany, France and at least six other EU countries oppose the term 'associate membership' for closer EU ties with Canada, ahead of the EU-Canada summit on 29–30 October. The disagreement over terminology highlights political sensitivities in EU external relations and could delay or reshape the proposed cooperation framework.

Turkey and Armenia agree student exchanges amid hopes of border reopening

EUalive

Turkey and Armenia agreed to expand academic cooperation with university student exchanges, as Armenia signals progress toward reopening its border with Turkey. The agreement marks a step in normalising relations between the two countries, with potential broader implications for regional stability and educational collaboration.

The Trans-Caspian cable: a historic breakthrough on the digital Silk Road

EUalive

The Trans-Caspian subsea fibre-optic cable between Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan has been laid, overcoming long-standing barriers to trans-Caspian digital infrastructure and advancing the TASIM project. The cable represents a significant development in international digital connectivity, with strategic implications for Europe-Asia data links.

published.title: Tech and Science, 21 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Israeli spyware targeted Belgrade university rector amid Serbia protests

EUalive

Israeli Pegasus spyware was used to infect the phone of the rector of the University of Belgrade, Vladan Đokić, a supporter of student protests against Serbia’s government. The targeting of a university leader with state-grade surveillance tools during an election period raises concerns about academic freedom and the suppression of dissent in Serbia.

Socialists push for EU law on deepfakes

Technology – POLITICO

The Socialists and Democrats group in the European Parliament is pushing for an EU-wide law to ban harmful deepfakes and require platforms to prevent their spread. The proposal addresses growing fears over AI-generated disinformation and the erosion of trust in digital media, with cross-border implications for regulation and enforcement.

NATO steps up Black Sea surveillance as attacks on shipping escalate

EUalive

NATO is deploying additional surveillance and intelligence assets in the Black Sea after attacks on commercial vessels off Bulgaria and Romania, including a US P-8 Poseidon aircraft for intelligence gathering. The escalation in maritime attacks and NATO’s response highlights the strategic importance of the Black Sea for European security and trade routes.

U.S. envoy Witkoff to meet Putin, Trump presses Kyiv to settle

EUalive

US envoy Steve Witkoff will meet Vladimir Putin after talks with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo, as Donald Trump urges Ukraine to end the war and withholds military support. The shifting US stance under Trump and the push for direct negotiations reshape the geopolitical calculus for Ukraine and its European allies.

Independent media under hacker attacks as report exposes coordinated effort favouring Vučić

EUalive

Independent Serbian media outlets N1 and Nova.rs face coordinated inauthentic network attacks amplifying pro-government messages and discrediting their reporting ahead of the 25 October elections. The systematic digital interference against independent media underscores the threats to press freedom and democratic processes in Serbia.

EU recasts Arctic policy around defence and critical infrastructure

EUalive

The European Commission’s new Arctic strategy prioritises defence, critical infrastructure and satellite surveillance in response to Russia’s military buildup and China’s resource ambitions. The policy shift reflects the EU’s growing security concerns in the High North, where climate change and geopolitical competition are reshaping strategic priorities.

published.title: Tech and Science, 19 October (mistral)
published.html:
Tech and Science

Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

A cyberattack forced hundreds of French supermarkets, including Intermarché and Carrefour, to discard defrosted food after hackers remotely raised refrigerator temperatures. The incident triggered EU-level coordination and exposed vulnerabilities in critical supply chains, raising questions about digital resilience in essential services.

Lithuania links failed Starlink arson attempt to Russian sabotage, citing Pattern with Poland and Bulgaria

EUalive

Lithuania linked a failed arson attempt on a Starlink equipment storage site to a Russian sabotage campaign targeting infrastructure supporting Ukraine. The attack follows similar incidents in Poland and Bulgaria, highlighting a coordinated effort to disrupt military communications and test EU digital and physical security.

published.title: Tech and Science, 19 October (anthropic)
published.html:
Tech and Science

Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

A cyberattack remotely raised the temperature in refrigerators at hundreds of French supermarkets including Intermarché and Carrefour, forcing retailers to destroy spoiled food and prompting Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to coordinate an EU-level response. Cybersecurity experts say the incident shows old-fashioned infrastructure vulnerabilities, not AI risk, matter more for food security than the AI-safety debate suggests.

France riots: Presidential hopeful Attal pitches social media blackout

Technology – POLITICO

French presidential hopeful Gabriel Attal has renewed his call to give the government power to temporarily block social media access in areas hit by rioting, following nationwide unrest that saw around 2,000 arrests. A mainstream candidate is proposing selective platform blackouts as a riot-control tool, a concrete test of how far digital speech restrictions could go in a major EU democracy.

Serbian prosecutor probing Trump Tower in Belgrade targeted with spyware

Cybersecurity and Data Protection – POLITICO

A Serbian prosecutor investigating alleged corruption around a Trump-linked Belgrade tower project was found to have been targeted with Pegasus spyware, according to research by Citizen Lab and the SHARE Foundation. It adds a judicial official to a widening spyware scandal engulfing Serbia's opposition and civil society, raising fresh questions about surveillance accountability on the EU's doorstep.

Ukraine’s drone strikes on Russian data centres may change how we see disinformation

English – The Conversation

Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed Russian data centres belonging to Yandex and Sberbank, cutting Yandex traffic by 94% and disrupting search, email and financial services across Russia. The strikes turn physical data infrastructure into a military target and raise unresolved questions about what counts as 'digital sovereignty' and whether destroying servers can curb disinformation.

published.title: Tech and Science, 17 October (mistral)
published.html:
Tech and Science

Von der Leyen pitches AI as solution to reduce reporting for European businesses

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed using AI to implement an ‘only once’ business reporting rule, letting companies submit data once for reuse by public administrations. The plan ties AI adoption to a concrete EU policy change that reduces administrative burdens on businesses across the bloc.

The EU shelved AI liability rules. Sam Altman has revived the debate.

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

EU parliamentarians are reviving calls for an AI liability law after OpenAI’s Sam Altman said companies should be responsible for harms caused by their models. The debate directly affects governance and accountability for AI in Europe, with potential legislative consequences.

Europe’s AI policing plan stokes privacy concerns

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

Senior EU officials warn that plans to expand Europol’s AI powers and double its budget to €3 billion raise significant privacy concerns. The proposal intersects AI adoption, law enforcement, and digital rights, with high stakes for oversight and civil liberties.

50 members of European Parliament targeted by deepfake porn, report says

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

A report finds that 50 MEPs, including 46 women, have been targeted by deepfake pornography, with one in six female MEPs affected. The scale of the issue highlights the urgent need for enforcement of AI-related protections and digital ethics in European institutions.

EU to offer single-market access to candidate countries

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

The EU will offer candidate countries gradual integration into the single market, including access to research programmes like Horizon Europe, while their accession is processed. This policy shift affects funding, research collaboration, and the strategic alignment of non-EU countries with EU programmes.

EU budget must bankroll Europe’s independence, von der Leyen says

Horizon Europe – POLITICO

Ursula von der Leyen argued the EU’s next seven-year budget must fund Europe’s independence from foreign powers, including investments in AI and strategic industries. The statement ties budget decisions to long-term research funding and technological sovereignty, a core EU priority.

published.title: Tech and Science, 17 October (anthropic)
published.html:
Tech and Science

Hungary poised to rejoin flagship EU research program

Research and Development – POLITICO

Hungary's science minister says the country has met all technical conditions to rejoin Horizon Europe, after restructuring university governance that had blocked funding under Viktor Orbán. Direct update on access to the EU's flagship research programme and the political conditions attached to it.

EU plans to expand Erasmus program to southern Mediterranean countries

Erasmus – POLITICO

The European Commission is extending Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe eligibility to students and researchers from southern Mediterranean countries as part of a new Pact for the Mediterranean, alongside a proposed doubling of the region's EU budget to €42 billion. A concrete programme expansion affecting two flagship EU funding schemes.

Huawei takes part in EU research programs despite Commission crackdown

Research and Development – POLITICO

Huawei is still taking part in 16 Horizon Europe-funded projects, including in cloud computing and 6G, despite the Commission formally restricting it as a high-risk supplier in 2023. Shows a gap between EU research funding rules and their enforcement, with security implications for partner universities and companies across several member states.

50 members of European Parliament targeted by deepfake porn, report says

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

A new report finds 50 members of the European Parliament, 46 of them women, have been targeted by AI-generated deepfake pornography, as the EU's ban on nudifier apps takes effect on 2 December. Puts a concrete number on AI-enabled gendered harm inside EU institutions and tests the bloc's ability to enforce its own new rules.

German search engine ditches Mistral, bets on Chinese open-source AI

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

German search engine Ecosia, used by institutions including Germany's environment ministry and the UK's NHS, has dropped France's Mistral as its AI provider in favour of open-source models, including Chinese ones, citing quality and reliability problems. A concrete case of a public-facing European digital service choosing non-European AI over the bloc's flagship champion, with implications for digital sovereignty claims.

Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI

Artificial Intelligence – POLITICO

European officials and executives are openly abandoning efforts to build competitive frontier AI models, arguing instead that Europe should focus on applying existing US and Chinese technology. Marks a quiet but significant shift in EU AI strategy away from building sovereign models and toward adoption, with direct consequences for funding priorities and industrial policy.

published.title: Tech and Science, 17 October (anthropic)
published.html:
Tech and Science

AI-Generated Hot Girls Are Ripping Off Comedians to Boost Their Horny Content

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

A network of AI-generated 'model' accounts is lifting material from stand-up comedians to drive traffic to paid OnlyFans and Fanvue profiles, with no real recourse for the comedians involved. Shows AI being used to exploit creative labour and divert audience attention and income from media-sector workers, a core concern for AI adoption in media.

Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

MIT professor Sherry Turkle argues that chatbots using first-person pronouns like 'I' and 'me' are fostering unhealthy emotional dependence in users. Raises a governance and design question about anthropomorphic AI interfaces and their psychological effects, relevant to AI ethics debates.

Podcast: Cops Can Use AI to Pinpoint Your Home with Just One Photo

404 Media

A 404 Media podcast examines Raven, an AI tool (formerly Geospy) that police can now use to pinpoint a specific house from a single interior photo, alongside a judge's ruling that a related Flock surveillance search was unconstitutional. Concerns AI surveillance capability and its legal limits, a governance issue with implications beyond the US context.

Here’s What Telegram Giving Data to the U.S. Government Looks Like

404 Media

Newly filed court records show the exact data, phone number, user ID and IP address, that Telegram handed over to US authorities for a specific user. Illustrates how a major messaging platform cooperates with government data requests, a digital ethics and privacy question with cross-border relevance.

published.title: Tech and Science, 16 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Council agrees to restore Horizon Europe, Erasmus+ funds for Hungary

Science Business

The EU Council voted on 13 October to end its rule-of-law conditionality mechanism against Hungary, restoring its access to Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ and releasing €4.2 billion in frozen cohesion funds. A direct reversal of EU funding policy restores Hungarian universities' and researchers' access to the bloc's main research and mobility programmes.

Zaharieva defends Commission’s research budget proposal

Science Business

EU research commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva told the Dublin AI summit that cutting the EU's research budget would be a strategic mistake, pushing back on the Irish presidency's proposed 9.6% cut. A sitting commissioner is openly contesting a Council proposal that would shrink the funding pool behind Horizon Europe.

Is the EU research budget actually increasing?

Science Business

A Science Business analysis unpacks whether the proposed €158 billion Horizon Europe budget amounts to a 10% cut or an increase, a dispute that has split opinion in Brussels. Clarifies the real figures behind competing political claims about the future size of the EU's main research funding programme.

Companies pledge free software and computing for AI in science

Science Business

The European Commission announced on 15 October that a group of companies and foundations will give European scientists free software and supercomputing access as part of its AI in Science Enablers Initiative. A concrete EU Commission programme shaping how researchers gain access to AI infrastructure.

EU auditors urge greater focus on research commercialisation

Science Business

The European Court of Auditors published a report on 15 October calling for EU funding of close-to-market research to focus more on commercialisation and better monitoring. An official audit finding that could reshape how future Horizon Europe-style funding is designed and evaluated.

Accenture Tells Employees They Can Now Spend Only $29 on Claude Per Month

404 Media

Accenture has told employees it will now cap spending on Anthropic's Claude at $29 per person per month, down from some cases of $1,000, as token costs spiral. A concrete case of a major employer curbing AI adoption after initial unlimited rollout, showing the real cost pressures behind corporate AI use.

published.title: Tech and Science, 14 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Research community to appeal to national governments over planned EU budget cut

Science Business

Brussels research lobby groups are rethinking their campaign strategy after the Council of the EU proposed a 9.6% cut to the research budget. Direct threat to the scale of Horizon Europe funding, with lobbies now shifting tactics to appeal to national governments.

Funding Radar: Horizon Europe opens €225M call for advanced materials and manufacturing

Science Business

Horizon Europe has opened a €224.7 million call for collaborative projects on chemicals, advanced materials and critical raw materials. A concrete, large funding call under Horizon Europe with a clear policy aim of strengthening European raw-materials capacity.

Lithuanian model could help Horizon Europe funds go further, says vice-minister

Science Business

Lithuania's vice-minister for education, science and sport is urging other EU countries to copy a national scheme that funds researchers who narrowly missed out on Horizon Europe grants. A concrete national fix for stretching scarce EU research money further, proposed as a model for wider adoption.

Data Corner: Public and private sectors take equal shares of Joint Undertaking funding

Science Business

A new data analysis finds that public and private sectors receive roughly equal shares of funding from the EU's Joint Undertakings, as negotiations to reshape these research partnerships intensify. Hard data feeding directly into the live debate over how Horizon Europe's partnership structures should be redesigned.

Viewpoint: The grant system funds the ability to apply for grants

Science Business

A London spatial-computing founder describes how his company's application to a major European innovation fund was rated highly on technical merit by evaluators but rejected for reasons unrelated to the technology. A first-hand account exposing how procedural and bureaucratic factors, not innovation quality, can decide EU grant outcomes.

OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

OpenAI and Anthropic executives told a UK parliamentary committee they want government regulation of AI, on the same day Britain's spy chief warned AI could be used to create bioweapons. Major AI developers publicly calling for binding rules, set against an official warning about catastrophic misuse risks.

published.title: Tech and Science, 12 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Council floats 9.6% budget cut to next Horizon Europe

Science Business

The Irish Council presidency has proposed cutting the next Horizon Europe budget by 9.6%, a €16.8 billion reduction from the Commission's €175 billion proposal. A direct cut to the EU's main research funding programme, affecting future grant availability for universities and research centres across Europe.

EIT approves seven-year strategic agenda for EIT Water

Science Business

The European Institute of Innovation and Technology has approved the seven-year strategic agenda for EIT Water, its newest Knowledge and Innovation Community, running from 2027 to 2033. Sets the direction for a new EU innovation funding stream ahead of a partnership agreement later this year.

University of Twente announces two new medtech collaborations with industry

Science Business

The University of Twente, together with TNO, has been awarded two new drug development projects through its Joint Innovation Centre BIO/MicroSystems in collaboration with industry partners. A Dutch university expanding applied research funding and industry ties in medical technology.

Trinity College Dublin: Experts examine how Ireland can strengthen resilience while driving growth during its EU Presidency

Science Business

Government, industry and EU officials met at Trinity College Dublin to discuss how Ireland can strengthen cyber resilience while holding the EU Council presidency. Links an EU presidency's policy priorities to cyber regulation and research resilience, relevant to EU research governance.

AI Company Lets Cops Pinpoint Specific Houses Based on a Single Interior Photo

404 Media

Graylark Technologies' Raven tool now lets police identify the exact address of a home from a single interior photo, pulling data from sites like Zillow and Airbnb, and is already used by LAPD and Miami-Dade police. Raises concrete governance and privacy questions about unregulated AI surveillance tools sold to law enforcement.

published.title: Tech and Science, 10 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

Staff at three major publishing houses told WIRED that executives are pushing increased use of large language models for publicity copy, cover art, back-cover blurbs and emails, with junior employees pressured to champion the tools. Direct evidence of AI adoption inside a media sector, including labour pushback from staff, matching the profile's focus on AI adoption in media and its effects on workers.

published.title: Tech and Science, 9 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

European Open Science Cloud Federation opens for business

Science Business

The European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) Federation has opened to the public, giving researchers easier access to data repositories from more than 200 research organisations across Europe. A decade-long EU research infrastructure project now live, directly affecting how European researchers share and access data.

Concern after Europeans endorse US science agenda

Science Business

Germany's largest research funder has voiced concern after Berlin and 15 other countries, including several in Europe, endorsed a US-led science policy statement called the Kyoto Vision. Signals a shift in European research policy alignment with Washington, raising questions about research autonomy.

EU governments to debate a 19-partnership Horizon Europe portfolio

Science Business

EU research ministers will meet on 12-13 October in Dublin to discuss a proposed portfolio of 19 partnerships for the next phase of Horizon Europe. A concrete decision point shaping which research areas get funded under Horizon Europe's successor programme.

Parliament stands firm on budget as Council readies negotiating box

Science Business

The European Parliament is holding firm on its budget demands as the Council prepares a revised negotiating position on the 2028-34 Multiannual Financial Framework, amending the €1.73 trillion June proposal with likely cuts. The MFF outcome will determine the funding envelope available for Horizon Europe and other EU research programmes.

Tristan Harris’ Tech Nonprofit Is Laying Off Most Staff and Going ‘Founder-Led’

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

The Center for Humane Technology, the nonprofit co-founded by Tristan Harris that helped spark concern over excessive screen time, is laying off most of its staff and shifting to a 'founder-led' model after internal disputes over strategy. A prominent digital-ethics watchdog is scaling back just as AI governance debates intensify.

Anthropic’s Quest to Give A.I. Morals

NYT > Technology

A new account details Anthropic's internal effort to build moral reasoning and values into its AI models, describing the work as part research, part evangelism. Offers a rare look inside how a major AI lab approaches ethics and governance rather than pure capability building.

published.title: Tech and Science, 7 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

MSCA research career scheme gets €210M funding boost

Science Business

The European Commission has added €240 million to the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) scheme, which funds doctoral and postdoctoral research training across Europe. Direct Horizon Europe funding decision affecting researchers and institutions, though the boost is expected to have limited impact on already low success rates.

Data Corner: The EU’s research and innovation performance in six charts

Science Business

A new European Commission report, visualised in six charts, shows the EU still lagging global competitors on research and innovation performance. Official EU policy assessment that frames future funding priorities and benchmarks European research output against the US and China.

The Netherlands unveils its new innovation agency

Science Business

The Netherlands has launched a new innovation agency, Nadi (National Agency for Disruptive Innovation), with a €500 million budget over ten years to fund competitions between inventor teams. A significant new national research funding structure in the Netherlands, joining a wave of similar European agencies modelled on ARPA-style funding.

Funding Radar: Horizon Europe opens new €35M call for climate-related projects

Science Business

The European Commission is opening three Horizon Europe calls on 6 October worth a combined €35 million for large-scale climate action projects, including a €20 million scheme to sub-grant smaller climate projects. A concrete, dated Horizon Europe funding call with specific budget figures for climate research consortia.

arXiv Is Rate Limiting Submissions Because It Can’t Keep up With AI Slop

404 Media

arXiv is now limiting researchers to two submissions per month and three active submissions at a time, after AI-generated paper volumes overwhelmed its volunteer moderators. A direct governance response to AI's effect on scholarly publishing infrastructure, with submissions nearly doubling to over 40,000 a month since 2024.

published.title: Tech and Science, 5 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

Muse Creates Detailed Profiles of All Your Friends and Family

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

Meta's AI companion app Muse, downloaded by millions, builds detailed profiles of users' friends and family from their conversations and data. Raises direct questions about AI governance and privacy in a mass-adopted consumer product, relevant to AI ethics and access debates.

Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI

The Verge - Science coverage for subscribers | The Verge

An essay argues that the AI industry's core assumption, that brains are essentially computers, misunderstands human cognition and is reshaping culture in harmful ways. A non-technical critique of AI's cognitive and cultural effects, directly matching the ethics and governance angle on AI adoption.

Vinnova: Strong Swedish participation in new European effort on raw materials

Science Business

Swedish research organisations are involved in 129 of 314 proposals submitted to the first call of RAMP, the EU's new Raw Materials Partnership for the Green and Digital Transition under Horizon Europe, coordinating 56 of them. Concrete data on participation in a new Horizon Europe partnership, directly relevant to EU research funding programmes.

University College Dublin launches Infection Research Ireland to help tackle future pandemics

Science Business

University College Dublin has launched Infection Research Ireland, expanding its former Centre for Experimental Pathogen Host Research with a broader mandate to prepare for future pandemics. A university research centre restructuring with an expanded funding and research mission, relevant to applied research policy at European universities.

Queen's University Belfast to benefit from £11.7M boost for pharmaceutical innovation

Science Business

Queen's University Belfast will receive £11.7 million from UK Research and Innovation's Local Innovation Partnerships Fund to accelerate pharmaceutical innovation and help businesses bring products to market. A specific, named research funding decision affecting a university, with amount and funder identified.

INESC TEC and Efacec signed programme agreement, introducing new model for collaboration with industry

Science Business

INESC TEC and Portuguese energy company Efacec have renewed their three-decade partnership and launched a new collaboration model for industry engagement that INESC TEC plans to extend to other partners. Shows a European research centre restructuring how it works with industry, relevant to applied research funding and institutional policy.

published.title: Tech and Science, 2 October
published.html:
Tech and Science

EU must invest an extra €565B to reach its 3% R&D spending target

Science Business

A new European Commission report finds the EU needs an extra €565 billion in R&D investment to hit its target of spending 3% of GDP on research by the end of the decade. Directly quantifies the gap in EU research funding, the headline metric for the whole research funding system including Horizon Europe.

Horizon Europe 2027 plans updated with €507M in new calls

Science Business

The European Commission has added €507 million in new funding calls to Horizon Europe's 2026-27 programme, covering biodiversity and linking research to market deployment. A concrete, dated expansion of Horizon Europe funding calls relevant to anyone tracking programme opportunities.

Time lost to political haggling means lost momentum for research

Science Business

Dag Rune Olsen, president of the Young European Research Universities Network, warns that political delays in finalising the next Horizon Europe budget are costing universities momentum. Flags a concrete risk to continuity of EU research funding as the next Horizon Europe cycle is negotiated.

Dual-use restrictions risk holding back research, Nordic universities say

Science Business

University leaders from Norway, Denmark, Sweden and Finland argue that excluding dual-use research from Horizon Europe would be a mistake given rising security concerns on Europe's eastern border. A direct policy fight over what counts as eligible research under Horizon Europe, with real consequences for funded projects.

Key MEPs back dropping EU’s 20% chip market share target

Science Business

Two key MEPs say the European Parliament is unlikely to oppose dropping the EU's target of a 20% global chip market share, favouring specialisation in specific components instead. A concrete shift in EU industrial and research policy under the Chips Act 2.0, changing what the bloc aims to fund and build.

Health Care Workers Are Tired of Cleaning Up Palantir’s Mess

Feed: Artificial Intelligence Latest

Nurses and other staff at a major hospital network say Palantir's scheduling software, brought in to streamline operations, is instead causing errors and burnout. A rare on-the-ground account of AI adoption's labour effects in a healthcare organisation, rather than a vendor claim.

published.title: Tech and Science, 30 September
published.html:
Tech and Science

Exclusive: Commission offers three options for cutting back Horizon Europe industrial partnerships

Science Business

The European Commission has proposed three scenarios for cutting Horizon Europe's 60 industrial partnerships down to as few as 18, and is now putting the options to EU member states. A direct restructuring of Horizon Europe funding architecture, affecting how research and industry collaborations are financed across the EU.

Allow dual-use research in next Horizon Europe, research ministers urge MEPs

Science Business

Research ministers from the Nordic and Baltic states, plus Poland and Romania, have written to MEPs urging that dual-use (civil-military) research be permitted under the next Horizon Europe programme. A concrete policy push that could reshape what kinds of research the EU's flagship funding programme supports after 2027.

Funding Radar: La Caixa’s €22M fund for health research

Science Business

Spain's La Caixa Foundation has opened a €22 million call for biomedical and health research, open to both individual researchers and consortia at any stage from basic to clinical research. A specific, sizeable funding opportunity for health researchers across Europe.

Data Corner: Which European countries pay doctoral candidates the most?

Science Business

New comparative data shows PhD stipends across Europe range from €2,263 a year in Ukraine to €58,014 a year in Denmark. Concrete evidence of how unevenly doctoral candidates are funded across European research systems.

AI for tech transfer: small victories or a revolution?

Science Business

Universities are increasingly using generative AI for technology-transfer work such as summarising legal advice, checking contracts and patent searching. Shows AI adoption inside university administration rather than in the lab, with open questions about whether it changes outcomes or just paperwork.

KICs need leaner administration, EIT chairman says

Iedereen heeft ze nodig, niemand wil hen: in Israël lijkt een regering vormen zonder Palestijnen onmogelijk

De Standaard

Israël worstelt met regeringsvorming na verkiezingen, waarbij Palestijnse partijen onvermijdelijk lijken ondanks eerdere afwijzingen door Joodse partijen. De politieke impasse in Israël en de mogelijke rol van Palestijnse partijen in een toekomstige regering zijn van groot geopolitiek belang.

Al voor de tweede keer dit jaar vallen in Spanje tientallen doden bij een treinongeval

De Standaard

Minstens 68 doden bij botsing tussen twee hogesnelheidstreinen in de Spaanse provincie Toledo. Een van de ergste treinrampen in Spanje dit jaar, met aanzienlijke menselijke en infrastructurele gevolgen.

Dieselprijs op recordhoogte: ‘Voor een halve dag diesel heeft Trump de Oekraïense veiligheid onder de bus gegooid’

Wereld - Knack

Dieselprijs in België bereikt recordhoogte van meer dan 2,50 euro per liter, mede door geopolitieke spanningen. De stijgende brandstofprijzen raken direct de portemonnee van burgers en bedrijven en hebben brede economische implicaties.

Winnaar Gouden Palm Panahi krijgt vijf jaar cel in Iran

De Standaard

Iraanse regisseur Jafar Panahi, winnaar van de Gouden Palm, veroordeeld tot vijf jaar cel en verbeurdverklaring van al zijn bezittingen. Een opvallende zaak die de onderdrukking van kritische stemmen in Iran benadrukt en internationale aandacht trekt.

Cyberaanval MyMinfin leidt tot uitstel belastingaangifte: “Ik kreeg een vreemde sms toen ik probeerde in te loggen”

De Standaard

Cyberaanval op MyMinfin leidt tot uitstel van belastingaangifte in België, met onduidelijkheid over de gegevens die hackers buitmaakten. Een belangrijke digitale veiligheidskwestie die directe gevolgen heeft voor burgers en de overheid.

Vooruit legt lat hoger voor De Wever en mikt op bijdrage van 1,5 miljard euro van de sterkste schouders

De Standaard

Vooruit eist 1,5 miljard euro bijdrage van de sterkste schouders in Vlaamse begrotingsonderhandelingen, terwijl ondernemers protesteren. De spanningen in de Vlaamse begrotingsdiscussie en de eisen aan ondernemers zijn van groot lokaal en economisch belang.

Dan toch geen ‘geassocieerd lidmaatschap’ voor Canada bij Europese Unie

Wereld - Knack

EU-lidstaten wijzen ‘geassocieerd lidmaatschap’ voor Canada af, ondanks eerdere gesprekken. Een belangrijke ontwikkeling in de EU-externe betrekkingen, met name de relatie met Canada.

Brussels burgemeester Close vraagt Von der Leyen zich te kanten tegen VS-sancties Internationaal Strafhof

De Standaard

Brusselse burgemeester Close en zeven andere Europese burgemeesters vragen Von der Leyen om zich uit te spreken tegen VS-sancties tegen het Internationaal Strafhof. Een opmerkelijke politieke actie die de spanningen tussen de EU, de VS en internationale rechtspraak belicht.

Wat nu? Vier opties voor het verdeelde Israël, dat nu al nieuwe verkiezingen ziet opdoemen

De Standaard

Israël ziet nieuwe verkiezingen opdoemen na onduidelijke verkiezingsuitslag en moeite om een regering te vormen. De politieke onzekerheid in Israël heeft directe gevolgen voor de stabiliteit in de regio en internationale betrekkingen.

Europese olieraffinaderijen maakten sinds begin van oorlog al 36 miljard euro extra winst: “Ze profiteren ervan om hun marges te verhogen”

De Standaard

Europese olieraffinaderijen boeken sinds het begin van de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten 36 miljard euro extra winst door verhoogde marges. De winststijging van raffinaderijen benadrukt de economische gevolgen van geopolitieke conflicten en de impact op energieprijzen.

Vlaamse universiteiten dienen klacht in tegen Europese Commissie: ze willen weten hoe ze samenwerkingen met Israël kunnen stopzetten

De Standaard

Vlaamse universiteiten dienen klacht in bij Europese Ombudsman over samenwerking met Israëlische instellingen in Horizon-programma. De kwestie raakt de ethische en politieke afwegingen binnen Europese onderzoeksfinanciering en de relatie met Israël.

Slechte opvolging, mank budgetbeheer en te veel consultants: audit Rekenhof is vernietigend over i-Police

De Standaard

Rekenhof kritisch over i-Police: slechte opvolging, mank budgetbeheer en te veel consultants, met oproep tot onderzoekscommissie. Het mislukte digitaliseringsproject van de politie toont structurele problemen in overheidsbeleid en -uitvoering.

Vlaamse uitgevers verzetten zich tegen AI en zullen actie voeren op Boektopia: “Het is eigenlijk het Wilde Westen”

De Standaard

Vlaamse uitgevers keren zich tegen AI-bedrijven die hun boeken zonder vergoeding gebruiken voor het trainen van modellen en waarschuwen voor de gevolgen voor de sector. De spanning tussen de creatieve sector en techgiganten over intellectueel eigendom en AI-training escaleert, met directe impact op de Vlaamse uitgeefwereld.

Had het kabinet-Verlinden een mol bij het Brusselse parket? Woordvoerders in verdenking gesteld voor lekken in zaak rond i-Police

De Standaard

Woordvoerders van het kabinet-Verlinden en het Brusselse parket worden verdacht van schending van het beroepsgeheim in de zaak rond i-Police. Een mogelijke inbreuk op de onafhankelijkheid van justitie door politieke actoren roept vragen op over de rechtsstaat in België.

Belgiumgate: grootschalige desinformatiecampagne tegen justitie en media ontmaskerd

Wereld - Knack

Een grootschalige desinformatiecampagne, gericht tegen de Belgische justitie en media zoals Knack en Le Soir, probeert het Qatargate-onderzoek te ondermijnen. De onthulling van een georganiseerde poging om het vertrouwen in justitie en pers te schaden is een bedreiging voor democratische instellingen.

Parlementsverkiezingen Israël: Netanyahu schakelt over op paniekmodus

Wereld - Knack

Israëlische premier Netanyahu verliest zijn meerderheid bij de parlementsverkiezingen, maar de oppositie zit klem door interne verdeeldheid. De onzekere uitslag in Israël kan leiden tot politieke instabiliteit in een cruciale regio, met mogelijke gevolgen voor de veiligheidssituatie.

Nu Vucic is verslagen: zal de Servische Studentenlijst er ook in slagen om te regeren?

Wereld - Knack

De Servische Studentenlijst wint de vervroegde parlementsverkiezingen, na massale protesten tegen president Vucic. Een historische overwinning voor een studentenbeweging in Servië kan de politieke dynamiek in de Balkan regio veranderen.

Europese pakjestaks neemt vliegende start: Chinese webwinkels doen Belgische schatkist rinkelen

Wereld - Knack

De Europese pakjestaks op goedkope e-commerce uit China brengt miljoenen op voor de Belgische schatkist, maar controle blijft een uitdaging. De impact van internationale handel en belastingmaatregelen op de Europese en Belgische economie is significant.

Iers besparingsplan voor Europa zet De Wever extra onder druk

Wereld - Knack

Ierland stelt een besparingsplan van 133 miljard euro voor de Europese begroting voor, wat druk zet op België. De discussie over de EU-begroting raakt directe Belgische belangen en de onderhandelingspositie van de regering.

Hete zomer levert Belgische aardbeientelers zure rekening op

De Standaard

Belgische aardbeientelers lijden onder de gevolgen van de hete zomer, met kleine oogsten en lage prijzen als resultaat. De landbouwsector in Vlaanderen kampt met structurele uitdagingen door klimaatverandering, met directe economische gevolgen.

Twee hogesnelheidstreinen botsen op elkaar in Spaanse provincie Toledo, al minstens dertig doden: “Het wordt een enorme tragedie”

De Standaard

Twee hogesnelheidstreinen botsen in Spanje, met minstens dertig doden tot gevolg. Een zware treintragédie in Europa trekt internationale aandacht en roept vragen op over veiligheid in het spoornetwerk.

Brengt haar woordvoerder minister van Justitie Verlinden nu echt aan het wankelen?

De Standaard

Nieuwe onthullingen in de zaak i-Police brengen minister van Justitie Annelies Verlinden in verlegenheid en zetten haar positie onder druk. De politieke spanning rond justitiële zaken en de verantwoordelijkheid van de minister is een belangrijk thema in de Belgische politiek.

Noorwegen en Finland belden anderhalf uur met Poetin en dat wekt Europese ergernis op

De Standaard

Noorwegen en Finland voerden een telefoongesprek met Poetin, wat ergernis wekt bij andere Europese leiders. De eenzijdige diplomatieke stappen van individuele EU-lidstaten ten opzichte van Rusland kunnen de Europese eenheid ondermijnen.

Frontex krijgt meer geld en personeel om migranten sneller terug te sturen

De Standaard

Frontex krijgt meer middelen om migranten sneller terug te sturen, met een nieuwe snelle interventie-eenheid. De versterking van de Europese grenscontroles en migratiebeleid blijft een actueel en controversieel thema.
